design.input: integer codes x (post-quantizer, grid g = eps / 2^G), L per cycle; the v0.1.8 ingest quantizer is not in the RTL
design.configuration: fixed by the host (shape, T, G, predictor; no config search in hardware); eps bits and times / meta varints are host-composed header segments streamed through
design.scope: S4DI v1, rank 0, relations off, zero / last / linear hold, D <= 2^ADDR_W = 2048, G <= 16
design.microarchitecture: S0 accept + sync state read (L banks) -> S1 predict / residual / deadband / q / reconstruction / state write (1-cycle write forwarding) -> S2 varint sizing + event record write (double-buffered record memory, one record per beat with events) -> S3 layout decision; emitter: START (head) + sparse 1 event / cycle or dense W elements / cycle -> 16-byte output queue, W bytes / cycle

error_codes.6: register overflow (pred, residual or reconstruction leaves signed 32 bits)
error_codes.8: host header beat overruns its segment (or 0 / > W bytes)

design.cycle_count: from the start cycle (1) to the cycle done is observed, inclusive (testbench count); full rate = a code beat and a header beat offered every cycle and out_ready = 1

verdict.keeps_up: Only with L = 8 lanes. The encoder must read every input code (it cannot skip unchanged values like the event-driven decoder), so at L = 2 it is input-bound: env T64 takes 65911 cycles vs 28444 for the W = 2 decoder (2.3172×). L = 4: 36656 (1.2887×). L = 8: 29204 cycles (1.0267×), within 6.22% of the 2-bytes/cycle output bound. With ECP5 fmax estimates: L = 8 does not keep up (0.8486× the decoder's values/s), L = 4 does not, L = 2 does not.
verdict.bottleneck: L = 1..4: the code input (T × ceil(D / L) cycles; every element-frame is read, compared and written back). L = 8: the W = 2 output byte port (ceil(bytes / 2) cycles) plus one START cycle per frame and the frame-pair double buffer (frame t + 2 waits for frame t to be emitted). The per-element datapath has no multiplier. Clock: the ECP5 critical path (nextpnr, W = 2, L = 8) is S1: unregistered state-BRAM read -> 1-cycle write-forwarding mux -> predictor -> residual -> deadband compare / reconstruction -> overflow flag; the varint sizing (S2) and the record read (prefetch FIFO) were taken off the critical path in this version. Next step for fmax: a registered BRAM output stage with 2-deep forwarding.
verdict.loop: Encoder and decoder pipeline cleanly: env T64 end to end at L = 8 is 29986 cycles, 1.0268× the slower of the two standalone runs; the decoder drains a few cycles after the encoder's last byte.

comparison.energy: not measured; the only pJ figure in this report is the quoted v0.1.10 model estimate
